create.name: Zen Center of Denver
create.bio:
The Zen Center of Denver began in 1974 as the Denver Zen Center, an affiliate of Philip Kapleau's Rochester Zen Center meeting in a small house in Congress Park. It became independent in 1989, once Kapleau had given Danan Henry transmission and placed him in charge; Henry later trained for ten more years with Robert Aitken and became a Diamond Sangha teacher, so the centre carries both lineages, which mix Sōtō and Rinzai practice with koan study. Three of his heirs took over its spiritual direction, and today it is led by Karin Ryuku Kempe and Peggy Metta Sheehan; Kempe has also received transmission in the White Plum lineage. A team of assistant teachers works alongside them.

After owning a historic church in the Highlands for nearly two decades, the community built a new temple near the University of Denver, opened just before the pandemic. Sittings run most mornings and on two evenings a week, in the zendo and on Zoom. Newcomers start with a monthly Beginners' Night or a Saturday introductory seminar, and members can meet a teacher one to one. The year also brings day-long zazenkai, five- and seven-day sesshin that can be joined in person or online, recorded talks, a tea-ceremony group, community discussion circles and volunteer work, including dharma programmes in prisons.

courses.title: Beginners' Night and Intro to Zen Seminar
courses.description: Two ways in for newcomers: a monthly weeknight session with instruction in sitting postures and breath awareness, one round of zazen and walking meditation, and a follow-up question time; or a two-hour Saturday seminar with more time for posture, questions and meeting the teachers. Registration is needed.
courses.price: There is no set cost, but a donation of your choosing is much appreciated

courses.title: Rohatsu Sesshin 2026
courses.description: A week of intensive practice in the Denver zendo under its two spiritual directors, Karin Ryuku Kempe and Peggy Metta Sheehan, with zazen, private interviews, talks, chanting and formal vegetarian meals. It can be joined staying overnight, coming daily from home or on Zoom; first-time participants apply through the office.
courses.price: $315 for ZCD members and $385 for non-members

courses.title: Summer Sesshin 2027
courses.description: A five-day retreat under the centre's two spiritual directors, with zazen, interviews, teisho, chanting and formal meals, attended in person or online. Partial scholarships are available.
courses.price: $225 for ZCD members and $275 for non-members

courses.title: Membership
courses.description: Members affirm the centre as their place of practice and gain ongoing one-to-one instruction with a teacher, a first-year mentor among senior students, discounts on classes, and a vote in its governance. Hardship never bars anyone from joining.
courses.price: Most members contribute between $50 and $100 per month, with $75 per month recommended

courses.title: Zazenkai
courses.description: Days of extended practice with long blocks of sitting, a talk, chanting, walking meditation and a silent meal, for people with some experience of zazen.

free_resources.title: Recent dharma talks
free_resources.description: Recorded teisho and dharma talks by the centre's teachers on koans, Zen classics and everyday practice, free to play on its website.

free_resources.title: Daily zazen on Zoom
free_resources.description: All the centre's regular sittings are streamed on Zoom, with two mornings a week online only, so anyone can sit with the community from home without being a member.
